procs.t3: background current and current pulses control transfer of the melting wire a background current maintains the arc while short current peaks assist droplet detachment with suitable adjustment regular transfer with few short circuits is possible the power source coordinates pulse shape and wire feed through the selected synergic characteristic aluminium stainless steel and steel with an appropriate wire gas program useful for varying welding positions and where less spatter than conventional transfer is required first select the correct material wire diameter and shielding gas then adjust wire feed and arc correction a pulse characteristic does not replace joint preparation or checks of penetration and sidewall fusion

procs.d: A slower power variation is superimposed on the MIG/MAG pulse.
procs.t3: a slower power variation is superimposed on the mig mag pulse in addition to the fast pulses controlling droplet transfer phases of higher and lower power alternate this slower rhythm affects weld pool movement and the ripple pattern it can produce a regular tig like surface while still welding with a consumable wire electrode particularly for visible aluminium welds and recurring components where a consistent weld appearance matters the approved characteristic still determines which materials and wires are supported coordinate double pulse frequency power difference and travel speed moving too slowly can introduce considerable heat despite pulsing a regular ripple pattern alone does not prove sufficient penetration or a defect free weld

procs.d: MAHE process for productive pulse welding with a controllable arc.
procs.t3: mahe process for productive pulse welding with a controllable arc hyperpuls is a manufacturer specific mig mag pulse control process mahe describes it for fast welding and multipass work deposition rate and travel speed must be matched to achieve the required weld geometry and sidewall fusion production welds and multipass joints with a suitable characteristic particularly where process control needs further adjustment beyond a standard pulse program actual speed distortion and interpass temperature depend on the component hyperpuls and double pulse are different functions the exact combination and availability must be checked at the control panel

procs.d: A pulse function in the HyperMIG range for the specific production task.
procs.t3: a pulse function in the hypermig range for the specific production task mahe lists hyperspeedpuls in the equipment features of the hypermig x range the function name alone is insufficient for selection the available characteristic material and intended wire gas combination are needed to establish the appropriate operating point recurring production welds for which a suitable hypermig pulse solution is to be assessed a trial on the actual material shows whether speed weld shape and spatter behaviour suit the task check the panel software version and activated program before selection compare travel speed weld geometry finishing work and component temperature together during the trial this establishes the benefit for the specific production process

procs.d: Concentrated MIG/MAG arc for welding tasks requiring greater penetration.
procs.t3: concentrated mig mag arc for welding tasks requiring greater penetration hyperforce focuses on a forceful arc and deep penetration this is particularly relevant where reliable melting of the joint sidewalls is required whether joint preparation or the pass sequence can be changed must be established on the specific joint components requiring higher power and demanding joints where material position and characteristic are suitable the process can provide an alternative to a less concentrated arc setting torch angle stick out travel speed and joint opening strongly influence the result deep penetration does not replace a qualified pass sequence burn through and excessive heat input must still be assessed

procs.d: MAHE characteristic for heat-sensitive components and gap bridging.
procs.t3: mahe characteristic for heat sensitive components and gap bridging hypercold is designed for controlled heat input and a manageable weld pool mahe particularly identifies gap bridging tasks and root passes its benefit comes from the appropriate combination of characteristic power and torch movement thinner or distortion sensitive structures and joints with a controlled fit up gap suitability is assessed against material joint shape and thickness reduced heat input must not result in a lack of sidewall fusion adjust power and speed so that both component edges melt reliably a cooler setting guarantees neither distortion free parts nor unlimited gap bridging

procs.d: Task-specific MIG/MAG control for the joint root.
procs.t3: task specific mig mag control for the joint root in a root pass the joint root and both sidewalls must melt without the pool falling through uncontrollably hyperroot is part of mahe s cold root functions root gap root face thickness and accessible torch position are therefore considered together with the characteristic first passes in suitable butt joints and tasks with varying access the joint determines whether a reverse side pass backing or additional root protection is needed establish the permitted gap range on a test piece and assess the weld underside hyperroot does not replace required back purging or weld inspection the panel determines whether root is available separately or within a combined function

procs.d: Alternating hot and cool phases for vertical-up welds.
procs.t3: alternating hot and cool phases for vertical up welds hyperup automatically alternates between a higher power phase and a cooler process phase this supports weld pool formation and control during upward welding mahe describes vertical up welds using straight travel rather than the usual weaving movement vertical welds requiring repeatable pool formation and consistent torch movement the material and characteristic must suit the intended position establish phase settings weld cross section and travel speed on a test piece an excessively large pool can still sag with hyperup availability depends on the panel and where applicable program activation

procs.n: TriArc · Cold, Root and Force combined
procs.d: Dynamic characteristic with power-dependent arc behaviour.
procs.t1: triarc cold root and force combined
procs.t3: dynamic characteristic with power dependent arc behaviour mahe describes triarc as a dynamic arc that uses cold root or force behaviour according to the selected power range the three names refer to different priorities in process control not three independent arcs operating simultaneously tasks using different power ranges within the intended characteristic component thickness pass sequence and desired pool behaviour are considered together when selecting the process the available functions are checked on the specific power source and panel triarc does not imply automatic thickness detection or blanket approval for every welding task

procs.d: Combined characteristic for heat-controlled tasks and root passes.
procs.t3: combined characteristic for heat controlled tasks and root passes according to mahe twinarc combines cold and root behaviour depending on the power setting it is a control function for a single arc the name must not be equated with tandem welding using two wire electrodes melting simultaneously joints focused on manageable heat input and root pass formation application is defined through the available cold root characteristic gap root face and travel speed remain operator settings twinarc is not the same as the hypermig twin equipment version with two wire feeders

procs.n: TIG LF pulse · controlling the pool rhythm
procs.d: Slower current changes make melting and cooling phases clearly recognisable.
procs.t1: tig lf pulse controlling the pool rhythm
procs.t3: slower current changes make melting and cooling phases clearly recognisable in pulsed tig welding pulse current and base current alternate while the tungsten electrode remains non consumable at low pulse frequencies the changes can guide pool control and rhythmic filler rod addition mahe describes lf pulse particularly for controlled pool handling and positional welding manual welds heat sensitive edges and positions where a manageable pool is helpful filler addition and hand movement are coordinated with the selected rhythm set pulse current base current pulse duration ratio and frequency together a high base current or long pulse duration can substantially increase average current lf pulse is neither ac frequency nor a different ignition method

procs.n: TIG HF pulse · rapid current changes
procs.d: Rapid current pulses influence arc concentration and stability.
procs.t1: tig hf pulse rapid current changes
procs.t3: rapid current pulses influence arc concentration and stability at higher pulse frequencies current pulses follow too quickly to provide individual working rhythms for the hand instead the setting influences arc focus and pool behaviour hf pulse controls welding current during the weld hf ignition provides contactless arc starting precision tig welds and tasks requiring concentrated arc control mahe specifies pulsing up to 20 khz for beta dx pro and omega ax pro other equipment has its own specifications a higher frequency is not automatically a better setting pulse current base current and pulse duration ratio must suit the joint the syn versions with automatic pulse adjustment must not be equated with the manual functions of the pro panels

procs.d: MAHE control function to compensate for changing arc length.
procs.t3: mahe control function to compensate for changing arc length in manual tig welding variations in the electrode to workpiece distance change arc conditions according to mahe hyperarcactive is designed to compensate for these length changes and provide more consistent heat input it supports hand control rather than replacing it positional welding difficult to access joints and varying torch distances the function is particularly useful where maintaining a consistently short arc is difficult electrode preparation gas coverage and torch handling remain important hyperarcactive is a control function not a separate pulse program or automatic seam tracking

procs.d: Direct current for many steels; alternating current for typical aluminium applications.
procs.t1: tig ac dc polarity and balance
procs.t3: direct current for many steels alternating current for typical aluminium applications in conventional dc tig welding the electrode is negative ac is often used for aluminium the electrode positive phase assists oxide cleaning while the electrode negative phase supports heat input into the workpiece ac balance determines the ratio of these phases dc for suitable steel and stainless steel joints ac for many aluminium joints material condition filler and surface preparation determine the specific process choice balance and ac frequency are separate parameters balance changes the phase ratio while ac frequency changes the number of complete polarity cycles too much electrode positive time increases tungsten loading balance displays vary by machine do not transfer percentages without checking

procs.n: AC Wave · waveform and arc character
procs.d: Sine, trapezoidal and square waveforms change AC arc behaviour.
procs.t1: ac wave waveform and arc character
procs.t3: sine trapezoidal and square waveforms change ac arc behaviour the waveform describes how current changes over time during the ac phases mahe lists sine trapezoidal and square waveforms as selectable modulations different rates of current change alter arc character and noise they must be considered separately from pulse frequency and ac balance adjusting the arc to the joint shape desired weld width and personal torch handling during ac welding check the available waveforms at the panel and change only one setting at a time waveform selection does not replace choosing the correct current range or preparing a clean aluminium surface

procs.n: Mix TIG · combining AC and DC phases
procs.d: Automatic alternation between AC and DC periods during TIG welding.
procs.t1: mix tig combining ac and dc phases
procs.t3: automatic alternation between ac and dc periods during tig welding mix tig combines ac periods with dc periods this combines the cleaning action of ac with a different pattern of energy input during dc mahe particularly identifies this mode for aluminium in positional welding aluminium tasks requiring adjustment of the interaction between cleaning action pool control and heat input the ac dc proportions and their timing depend on the available program mix tig differs from ac balance within a single ac cycle and requires an appropriately equipped ac dc power source

procs.d: Spot and tacking functions support recurring short welds.
procs.t3: spot and tacking functions support recurring short welds hyperspot is mahe s function for localised tig welds activespot is additionally listed on hypertig ax and dx as a fast tacking function defined settings help position components for the subsequent weld the two functions are distinguished at the respective panel tacks on sheet assemblies and recurring joints where a consistent sequence of spots matters match current spot duration and cooling time to the material and joint gap gas pre flow and post flow also matter when tacking these tig functions are not resistance spot welding using electrode tongs

procs.d: Supporting equipment function, not a separate pulse or welding process.
procs.t3: supporting equipment function not a separate pulse or welding process mahe describes activeboost as a selectable power reserve related to available mains power and fuse protection the function concerns power delivery by the power source and must be distinguished from arc programs such as lf pulse hf pulse or mix tig tasks with temporarily increased power demand on appropriately equipped beta dx or omega ax versions select the mains connection fuse protection supply cable and duty cycle according to the equipment documentation activeboost permits neither an unchecked increase in fuse rating nor unlimited continuous power
